Pegasus. The legendary winged horse of Greek mythology, born from the blood of the slain Gorgon Medusa when she was beheaded by Perseus. This divine steed became the noble companion of the hero Bellerophon, enabling him to accomplish impossible feats, most famously the defeat of the Chimera. Pegasus transcends the role of mere beast, representing divine grace and the link between mortal heroism and celestial power.

He was born from Medusa's blood when Perseus decapitated her during a difficult quest, making him a creature tied to both death and divine grace, a paradox central to his meaning. A winged horse with pure white plumage, capable of flight and divine speed beyond mortal comprehension, embodying grace and nobility in equine form.

He was tamed and ridden by the hero Bellerophon, who used him to defeat the three-headed Chimera that plagued the kingdom of Lycia, proving Pegasus essential to heroic success. He created the spring Hippocrene on Mount Helicon with a single hoof strike, a spring sacred to the Muses, firmly associating Pegasus with poetry, inspiration, and artistic genius.

Eventually he transcended to the heavens, where Zeus transformed him into a constellation still bearing his name, immortalizing him in the night sky as eternal recognition of his deeds. In some accounts, Pegasus is said to belong to the Muses themselves, serving as a symbol of poetic genius and artistic transcendence that inspires mortal creativity. He is represented as the ideal of noble and divine power placed at the service of heroic virtue, a bridge between the divine realm and mortal accomplishment.

The image of Pegasus became an enduring symbol in Western art and literature, representing the marriage of power and beauty with creative inspiration. Medusa is the Gorgon from whose death Pegasus was born, linking nobility to monstrosity. Bellerophon is the hero who tamed and rode Pegasus to accomplish his legendary deeds. The Chimera is the three-headed monster defeated by Bellerophon mounted upon Pegasus. Poseidon is the god credited in some accounts with fathering Pegasus through Medusa. Echidna is the mother of both Medusa and the Chimera, making her distantly ancestral to Pegasus. Heracles is a fellow hero of legendary accomplishment, sharing the theme of divine-aided heroism. Athens is the city where Pegasus became an important symbol in art and architecture.
